title: GeoPace Course Bundle
description: Everything the app needs about one course, prepared by the Python pipeline. The single contract between pipeline and app. Bump schema_version on any breaking change.

generated_at.description: When the pipeline wrote this bundle, ISO-8601 with an explicit UTC offset.

course.description: Hand-maintained course facts, copied from data/courses/<id>/course.yaml.

timezone.description: IANA time zone name, e.g. Europe/Berlin.

km.description: Distance from the start along the course file, same scale as course_line.km.

editions.description: Hand-maintained edition facts, copied from data/courses/<id>/editions/<year>.yaml, oldest first. Sourced facts: what an organizer states. Neither measured nor subjective, and every one carries its source.

measured.description: Measured data, and values computed from it with published models (e.g. difficulty). Subjective data (forum reports etc.) never goes in here.

elevation_not_measured.description: Stretches where course_line.elevation_m (and so grade and difficulty) is not a measurement but a straight line between measured heights: a bridge deck the ground model leaves out, or a gap in the scan of one. In course order, never overlapping; empty when every height is measured. The app greys these stretches out instead of drawing them as measured.

km_start.description: km from the start, same scale as course_line.km.

reason.description: Shown to the runner: what stands there, and how the height was filled in.

white_model.description: The city's real buildings along this course, written beside this bundle as its own file (schema/white-model.schema.json). Absent for a course nobody has building data for; the app then draws the course on the plain map. The geometry is far larger than everything else about a course put together, so the bundle only names it and counts it — and carries its credits, which must be on screen whenever the buildings are.

file.description: The file's name, beside this bundle.

corridor_m.description: How far either side of the course a building had to be to be kept.

sun.description: Where the sun is through race day, and whether it reaches each course sample at the moment a runner gets there. Binary, never a share: a 10 m sample either has direct sun on it at that moment or it hasn't (PLAN.md D58). Absent for a course nobody has building data for, and then the app has no Sun layer. Only the steps whose sun stands at least floor_deg over `reference` are here — all of race day worth modelling, not only the race window, so a runner who types in their own start time is answered too. Outside those steps the app says the sun is down, or that it is too low to reach a city street, stated rather than worked out.

step_minutes.description: How far apart the steps are, in minutes.

first_step.description: The first step, ISO-8601 with its UTC offset in the course's time zone. The steps are evenly spaced in real time, so step t is this plus t * step_minutes.

steps.description: How many steps the table holds.

samples.description: How many course samples it holds: one row per course_line sample, in the same order.

floor_deg.description: The lowest sun shade was worked out for. Below it a city street is in shadow whatever anyone computes, so no step under it is here.

reference.description: Where altitude_deg and azimuth_deg are worked out: the start line. The table itself uses the sun at each sample's own place, a fifth of a degree away over 20 km of city.

altitude_deg.description: The sun's height over the reference place at each step, in degrees.

azimuth_deg.description: The sun's bearing at each step, degrees clockwise from true north.

bytes_per_sample.description: How many bytes one sample's row of steps takes: steps rounded up to a whole byte.

in_sun.description: One bit per sample and step, base64. Sample-major, so each sample's row starts on a byte: sample i at step t is bit (7 - t % 8) of byte i * bytes_per_sample + t // 8, and 1 means the sun reaches it. The spare bits at the end of a row are 0.

buildings.description: What the shade was worked out from. A wider set than the White model draws and never shipped: a tall building reaches the course from far outside the drawn corridor, so beyond `within_m` a building is kept only if its height is at least its distance divided by `reach_per_meter`.

counted.description: How many buildings could reach the course at all.

within_m.description: Inside this, every building was kept whatever its height.

furthest_m.description: Nothing further away than this was asked for.

reach_per_meter.description: How far a metre of building reaches at the floor: 1 / tan(floor_deg).

sources.description: Every dataset the bundle was built from.

attributions.description: Credits the app must show whenever this bundle's data is on screen.

edition.description: One year's running of the course: its date and its waves.

if.description: A carried-over wave needs the edition to say from which edition, and why.

edition.description: Which edition: the calendar year it is run in.

day.description: Local calendar date of the race in course.timezone.

confirmed.description: false when the organizer hasn't stated this edition's date and it is known another way; the note then says how, and the app says so next to the date.

note.description: Shown to the runner, e.g. how the date is known.

carried_over.description: Present when some details are copied from an earlier edition because this year's aren't published yet. The app must flag every carried-over detail to the runner, with the reason.

waves.description: At least one wave has a start time: without one there is no race clock to run.

wave.description: A group of runners with its own start time.

if.description: A wave has both its wall-clock time and the instant it means, or neither; and with neither, a note saying why and nothing to carry over.

start_local.description: Wall-clock start time in course.timezone, HH:MM, as the organizer prints it. null when the organizer hasn't published this wave's time: never a guess.

start.description: The same moment as ISO-8601 with its UTC offset, worked out by the pipeline in course.timezone (so a daylight-saving change is already applied). null exactly when start_local is.

carried_over.description: true when this wave's time is copied from the edition named in the edition's carried_over.

note.description: Shown to the runner. Always present when there is no start time, to say why.

course_line.description: The course resampled at a fixed spacing. Columns are parallel arrays: index i of every column describes the same sample. The last sample is the finish, so its spacing to the previous one can be shorter.

km.description: Distance from the start in km.

elevation_m.description: Terrain-corrected, smoothed elevation in meters above sea level (the ground model's vertical datum).

ellipsoid_height_m.description: The same height in meters above the WGS84 ellipsoid, which is where a 3D globe counts heights from: elevation_m plus the geoid model's offset at that place (the model is listed in sources). The two differ by tens of meters, by a different amount in each city. The app draws the course at this height where a photographed city stands over the road.

grade.description: Rise over run of the smoothed elevation (0.05 = 5% uphill).

difficulty.description: Energy cost of running at this grade relative to flat ground (1 = flat). null where the grade is outside the model's valid range.

bearing_deg.description: Direction of travel in degrees clockwise from true north.
